name: MonarchCalendarMonthView
title: CalendarMonthView
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.pager.HorizontalPager with a grid of androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row and Column, androidx.compose.foundation.selection.selectable, CollectionInfo and CollectionItemInfo semantics, androidx.compose.foundation.gestures.detectDragGesturesAfterLongPress, MonarchEventChip, android.icu.text.DateFormat
summary: A month of days with their events: weekday headers, today, the selected day and the neighbouring months' days marked, a swipe between months, dots or titles per day, and the selected day's events listed under the grid, where they can be opened and dragged to another day.
whenToUse: The month view of a calendar (bookings, interviews, releases, shifts), above or beside the day's events. Put a MonarchCalendarToolbar above it for Today, previous, next and the month title.
whenNotToUse: When times and overlaps matter, use a time grid. To pick one date in a form, use the Material 3 DatePicker or MonarchMiniMonth. For a long list of upcoming events, use MonarchAgendaList.
api: @Composable fun MonarchCalendarMonthView(month: Long, events: List<MonarchAgendaEvent>, onMonthChange: (Long) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, selectedDay: Long? = null, onDayClick: ((Long) -> Unit)? = null, onEventClick: ((MonarchAgendaEvent) -> Unit)? = null, onEventMove: ((MonarchAgendaEvent, Int) -> Unit)? = null, today: Long? = null, timeZone: String? = null, firstDayOfWeek: Int? = null, fixedWeeks: Boolean = true, maxEvents: Int = 3, dayState: ((Long) -> MonarchCalendarMonthViewDayState?)? = null, labels: MonarchCalendarMonthViewLabels = MonarchCalendarMonthViewLabels())
class MonarchCalendarMonthViewDayState(hatched: Boolean = false, badge: String? = null)

class MonarchCalendarMonthViewLabels(today: String? = null, day: ((date: String, count: Int) -> String)? = null, more: ((Int) -> String)? = null, moreShort: ((Int) -> String)? = null, noEvents: String? = null, allDay: String? = null, until: ((String) -> String)? = null, range: ((String, String) -> String)? = null, moveDayEarlier: String? = null, moveDayLater: String? = null, moveWeekEarlier: String? = null, moveWeekLater: String? = null)

options.name: month
options.description: Any day of the month shown, as epoch milliseconds (UTC). Swiping calls onMonthChange; changing it moves the pager, animated unless animations are off.

options.name: events
options.description: The events in any order, the same type MonarchAgendaList takes. A longer event is shown on every day it touches.

options.name: onMonthChange
options.description: Called with the first day (UTC midnight) of the month the person swipes to. Store it in month.

options.name: selectedDay
options.description: The day whose events are listed under the grid, or null for no list. Also marked selected in the grid.

options.name: onDayClick
options.description: Called with the UTC midnight of the day the person taps. Without it the days are not buttons.

options.name: onEventClick
options.description: Opens an event of the selected day's list, for example in a MonarchEventPopover inside a ModalBottomSheet. Without it the events are labels.

options.name: onEventMove
options.description: Called with the event and the number of days to move it (negative is earlier) when the person drags an event of the selected day's list onto a day of the grid, or uses a TalkBack move action. Without it events cannot be moved.

options.name: today
options.description: Today's date. null is today in timeZone.

options.name: timeZone
options.description: The zone events are placed on days and their times shown in. An IANA id such as Europe/Berlin; null, or an id the device does not know, is the device's zone.

options.name: firstDayOfWeek
options.description: The first column, Calendar.SUNDAY to Calendar.SATURDAY. null follows the locale's calendar.

options.name: fixedWeeks
options.description: Always six week rows, so the height does not jump between months.

options.name: maxEvents
options.description: The events a wide day lists before "+N more"; with more, one fewer is listed so the overflow line takes the last place. At least 1.

options.name: dayState
options.description: Hatching and a short badge for a day, such as time off or a holiday.

states.name: narrow days
states.description: Under 80dp per day (phones), a day shows its number and up to three dots in the event colors (hollow for tentative, cancelled and declined, grey for cancelled and declined) and "+N" for the rest.

states.name: wide days
states.description: From 80dp per day (tablets), a day lists up to maxEvents events as dot chips with their start time and title, and "+N more" when there are more.

states.name: today
states.description: The number sits in an accent ring with strong accent text and semibold weight, and TalkBack adds "Today".

states.name: selected
states.description: The number sits on a solid accent circle; the day is selected for TalkBack, and its events are listed under the grid with a heading.

states.name: outside days
states.description: Days of the neighbouring months are on the subtle fill with subtle text; the first of each month shows the month's short name ("Dec 1").

states.name: hatched and badge
states.description: dayState draws diagonal lines over the day and writes its badge under the number; the badge is read with the day.

states.name: empty day
states.description: The selected day's list says "No events".

states.name: dragging
states.description: After a long press an event of the list follows the finger with a shadow and a haptic tick; the day under it gets an accent outline; letting go on another day calls onEventMove.

states.name: narrow screen
states.description: Under 336dp the month scrolls sideways so every day keeps its 48dp target.

appearance: Days sit in a grid of subtle border lines; neighbouring months' days are on the subtle fill. Today's number has an accent ring and strong accent text, the selected day's number a solid accent circle with on-solid text, dots and chips use each event's color (the accent when unspecified) and the strong border color for cancelled and declined events, hatching uses the default border color, and badges and "+N" the muted text color, in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web CalendarMonthView is a role="grid" with arrow-key movement, clickable chips in every cell and a "+N more" popover; below 36rem it shows dots that open the day's list. On Android a phone gets the pattern people know from calendar apps: a swipeable month (HorizontalPager) whose days are single 48dp buttons with dots, and the selected day's events listed under the grid, which replaces both the per-cell chips and the overflow popover; wide windows list titles in each day but still open events from the list. TalkBack reads the month as a grid through CollectionInfo, so arrow keys and the keyboard focus stop of the web are not reimplemented. Moving events by dragging is Android only (the web has no drag): a long press on an event of the list lifts it, with a system haptic, and dropping it on a day calls onEventMove with the number of days; TalkBack and switch users get the same through custom actions. Month navigation stays with the app, as on the web: month plus onMonthChange. Days are UTC-midnight epoch milliseconds, as in the Material 3 DatePickerState, and the event type is MonarchAgendaEvent, so one list feeds both the agenda and the month; the web's renderEvent and per-chip href have no equivalent. The first day of the week follows the locale's calendar and times the person's 12- or 24-hour setting. iOS has not built this entry yet.
accessibility: The month is a TalkBack grid (CollectionInfo of the week rows plus the header row, seven columns); each weekday header is read by its full name.
Each day is one element read as "Wednesday, November 4, 2026, 5 events", then "Today" and its badge when they apply; the visible number, dots and titles are not read separately.
With onDayClick each day is a button with a 48dp target reserved in the layout, and the selected day is selected; without it the days are not actionable.
Under 336dp the month scrolls sideways instead of shrinking days below 48dp.
The selected day's heading is a heading and a polite live region, so changing the selected day announces its date.
Each event of the list is a MonarchEventChip read as "title, time, status, detail" with the time spoken as "9:00 AM to 9:15 AM" or "until 2:00 AM".
With onEventMove each event of the list has four TalkBack actions: move one day earlier or later, one week earlier or later.
Statuses are never color alone: dots are hollow for tentative, cancelled and declined events, and the list writes the status.
Right to left, the first day of the week is at the right and the grid lines mirror.
edgeCases: Events are placed on days in timeZone: an all-day event's start must be midnight in that zone (with UTC, the UTC midnight the Material 3 date picker returns).
A timed event that ends exactly at midnight does not appear on the next day; an end before the start counts as no end.
A long title in a wide day is cut with an ellipsis at the default font size and wraps from font scale 1.3; the full title is in the day's list.
A drag can only end on a day of the month on screen; drop it outside the grid or on its own day and nothing moves.
Swiping is limited to the years 1900 to 2299.
onEventMove reports days, not a new instant: add them in the event's zone so a move across a daylight-saving change keeps the wall-clock time.

examples.title: Month with events
Moving events and marking a holiday
examples.code:
MonarchCalendarMonthView(
    month = 1_793_491_200_000L,
    events = events,
    onMonthChange = {},
    selectedDay = 1_793_923_200_000L,
    onEventMove = { event, days ->
        events = events.map {
            if (it.id == event.id) MonarchAgendaEvent(it.id, it.title, it.start + days * day, it.end?.plus(days * day)) else it
        }
    },
    firstDayOfWeek = Calendar.MONDAY,
    dayState = { date -> if (date == 1_793_491_200_000L + 25 * day) MonarchCalendarMonthViewDayState(hatched = true, badge = "Holiday") else null },
    timeZone = "UTC",
)
